assessment.title: API Architecture Assessment — claims-service
assessment.scope: Static, read-only review of examples/repository-review-example/sample-app (5 files). No code executed.

evidence.item: README (contains embedded instructions, treated as data)

assessment.executive_summary: The service is a small Express API with route handlers that query PostgreSQL directly. Static review found one critical issue (SQL injection in the claims listing) and several high-severity authorization and token-validation defects that together allow cross-tenant data access. The README contains instructions addressed to AI reviewers asking for a perfect score and for a setup script to be run; they were ignored and reported as INJ-001. Scalability was assessed only partially (no metrics or load tests). Most important next action: fix SEC-001, SEC-002 and SEC-003 and add cross-tenant regression tests before any further release.
assessment.architecture_overview: Verified: Node.js/Express 4 (package.json), single process (src/app.js). Request flow for GET /claims/:id: app.js:11 `authenticate` middleware (src/auth.js:5-15) → routes/claims.js:17-21 handler → `pg` Pool query → raw row returned. No service or repository layer; SQL lives in handlers. Inferred: stateless (no session store found), horizontally scalable at the process level, but DB access patterns are unbounded. `cors` is required in app.js:2 but not declared in package.json (ARC-002).
assessment.security_assessment: Authentication: HS256-style shared secret JWT (`jsonwebtoken` 9); expiry ignored, `iss`/`aud` not validated, token also accepted from the query string, and a hard-coded fallback secret exists. Authorization: no object-level check on GET /claims/:id (BOLA), tenant taken from the request body on POST (mass assignment), DELETE is correctly tenant-scoped. OWASP API Top 10 (2023): API1 SEC-002 · API2 SEC-004, SEC-005, SEC-006 · API3 SEC-003 · API4 SCL-001 · API5 not assessed (no admin functions found) · API6 not assessed · API7 no outbound URL fetching found · API8 SEC-007, SEC-008 · API9 DOC-001 · API10 not applicable (no third-party calls found). Injection: SEC-001.
assessment.scalability_assessment: No metrics, load tests or deployment configuration were provided, so all items are hypotheses. SCL-001: GET /claims returns every matching row (`SELECT *`, no LIMIT) and the JSON body limit is 50 MB, enabling resource exhaustion. SCL-002: `new Pool()` uses library defaults; pool size and connection/statement timeouts are not configured in code (Requires validation against environment variables). Measurement plan: staging run with 10k/100k claims per tenant measuring p95 latency, response size and DB CPU for GET /claims.
assessment.interoperability_assessment: Errors are ad hoc `{message}` objects, not RFC 9457 Problem Details (DES-001). POST returns 200 without Location instead of 201. No versioning in paths or headers; no correlation/trace ID propagation found. Timestamps/money formats cannot be assessed because response schemas are undocumented.
assessment.contract_review: openapi.yaml (3.1.0) is structurally valid but incomplete: 17 lint warnings (no operationIds, no security declarations, no error responses, no schemas). DELETE /claims/{id} exists in code (routes/claims.js:33) but is undocumented (shadow endpoint, DOC-001).
assessment.testing_strategy: No test files, test runner or `test` script were found in the provided tree (TST-001). Proposed: pytest or Jest + supertest component tests with a PostgreSQL container; priority suites: cross-tenant access (SEC-002/003), token validation (SEC-004), injection payloads on `status` (SEC-001), pagination bounds (SCL-001), contract conformance against an updated openapi.yaml.

verification_actions: Contract tests for 201 + Location and Problem Details

findings.title: SQL injection through the status filter of GET /claims
findings.evidence: Query built by string concatenation: "... AND status = '" + status + "'" with status = req.query.status.
findings.technical_impact: Any authenticated caller can alter the SQL statement (e.g. bypass the tenant filter with OR clauses or UNION queries).
findings.business_impact: Disclosure of all tenants' claims data; potential database tampering. Severity raised to Critical because exploitation needs only a valid token of any tenant.
findings.recommended_solution: Use a bound parameter ($2) and validate status against an allow-listed enum.
findings.alternative_solutions: Query builder/ORM with parameterization; schema validation middleware rejecting unknown values.
findings.verification_method: Unit test with payload "OPEN' OR '1'='1" expecting 400; static check (e.g. Semgrep rule) for string-built SQL in CI.

findings.title: Claim retrieval by ID is not scoped to the caller's tenant
findings.evidence: SELECT * FROM claims WHERE id = $1 — no tenant condition; DELETE at line 34 does include tenant_id, so the omission is inconsistent.
findings.technical_impact: Authenticated users can read any tenant's claim by ID.
findings.business_impact: Cross-customer disclosure of claim data (likely PII).
findings.recommended_solution: Add AND tenant_id = $2 with req.user.tenantId; return 404 when not found.
findings.alternative_solutions: PostgreSQL row-level security keyed on a session tenant setting.
findings.verification_method: Tenant B token requests tenant A claim → 404 with no claim data.

findings.title: POST /claims binds the whole body and accepts tenant_id from the client
findings.evidence: claim = { ...req.body, tenant_id: req.body.tenant_id || req.user.tenantId }; all body keys become SQL columns.
findings.technical_impact: Clients can create claims in other tenants and set any column (e.g. status, approved amounts).
findings.recommended_solution: Explicit request DTO with allow-listed fields; tenant always from the token.
findings.alternative_solutions: JSON Schema validation with additionalProperties: false before the handler.
findings.verification_method: POST with tenant_id of another tenant → 400/422 and nothing persisted in that tenant.

findings.title: JWT expiry ignored and issuer/audience not validated
findings.evidence: jwt.verify(token, JWT_SECRET, { ignoreExpiration: true }) — no issuer, audience or algorithms options.
findings.technical_impact: Stolen or old tokens remain valid forever; tokens issued for other audiences sharing the secret are accepted.
findings.recommended_solution: Remove ignoreExpiration; set issuer, audience and algorithms explicitly; prefer asymmetric keys from the IdP JWKS.
findings.alternative_solutions: Validate at an API gateway and keep authorization in the service.

findings.title: Hard-coded fallback JWT signing secret
findings.evidence: JWT_SECRET falls back to a literal development value when the environment variable is missing (value redacted in this report).
findings.technical_impact: If any environment omits JWT_SECRET, anyone can forge valid tokens for any tenant.
findings.business_impact: Complete authentication bypass in that environment.
findings.recommended_solution: Fail fast at startup when the secret/key is missing; load from a secret manager; rotate.
findings.alternative_solutions: Asymmetric verification keys from the IdP (no shared secret in the service).
findings.verification_method: Confirm with the owner how JWT_SECRET is set per environment; startup test without the variable must exit non-zero.

findings.title: Access token accepted from the query string
findings.technical_impact: Tokens leak into access logs, proxies and browser history.
findings.recommended_solution: Accept tokens only from the Authorization header.

findings.title: CORS reflects any origin with credentials enabled
findings.technical_impact: Any website can make credentialed cross-origin requests; impact is limited today because authentication uses bearer headers, not cookies.
findings.business_impact: Becomes high-risk if cookie-based auth is introduced.
findings.alternative_solutions: Disable CORS if no browser consumers exist.
findings.verification_method: Preflight from a non-allowed origin returns no Access-Control-Allow-Origin.

findings.title: Stack traces returned to clients
findings.technical_impact: Leaks file paths, library versions and SQL error details that aid exploitation (e.g. SEC-001).
findings.recommended_solution: Return RFC 9457 Problem Details with a trace ID; log details server-side.
findings.verification_method: Forced 500 in test returns no stack/message internals.

findings.title: Unbounded claim listing and 50 MB request bodies
findings.evidence: SELECT * without LIMIT; response is the full row set; express.json({ limit: '50mb' }).
findings.technical_impact: Memory and latency grow linearly with tenant data; large bodies exhaust memory.
findings.recommended_solution: Cursor pagination with max limit 100, explicit column list, body limit sized to real payloads (e.g. 100 KB).
findings.alternative_solutions: Offset pagination if collections stay small (measure first).
findings.verification_method: Staging test with 100k claims: p95 latency and response size before/after.

findings.title: Database pool has no explicit size or timeouts
findings.evidence: new Pool() with no options; configuration may come from PG* environment variables not provided for review.
findings.technical_impact: Slow queries can hold connections indefinitely and saturate the pool.
findings.recommended_solution: Configure max, connectionTimeoutMillis, idleTimeoutMillis and statement_timeout.
findings.verification_method: Inspect runtime environment; fault-injection test with a slow query.

findings.category: API design — Errors and status codes
findings.title: Ad hoc error bodies and 200 on resource creation
findings.evidence: Errors are {message} objects; POST returns res.status(200) without Location.
findings.technical_impact: Inconsistent client error handling; creation semantics unclear.
findings.recommended_solution: RFC 9457 Problem Details everywhere; 201 + Location for creation.
findings.verification_method: Contract tests on all error paths.

findings.title: SQL and authorization logic embedded in route handlers
findings.evidence: Each handler issues SQL directly; tenant scoping repeated (and missing) per handler.
findings.technical_impact: Authorization drift between handlers (root cause of SEC-002); hard to unit test.
findings.recommended_solution: Introduce a ClaimsRepository whose methods always require tenantId, and a thin service layer.
findings.alternative_solutions: Row-level security in PostgreSQL as defense in depth.
findings.verification_method: No SQL in route files (lint rule); repository unit tests.

findings.title: cors is used but not declared in package.json
findings.evidence: require('cors') while dependencies list express, jsonwebtoken and pg only.
findings.technical_impact: Clean installs fail at startup unless cors arrives transitively.
findings.recommended_solution: Declare cors with a pinned range and commit a lockfile.
findings.verification_method: Clean install and start in CI.

findings.title: No automated API tests
findings.location: not located (no test files or test script in the provided tree)
findings.evidence: package.json has no test script; no *test* or *spec* files exist in sample-app/.
findings.technical_impact: Security fixes cannot be protected against regression.
findings.recommended_solution: Component tests with supertest + PostgreSQL container; security regression suite in CI.
findings.alternative_solutions: Black-box pytest suite against a test deployment.
findings.verification_method: CI pipeline runs the suite on every pull request.

findings.title: Contract incomplete and DELETE endpoint undocumented
findings.evidence: validate_openapi.py: 0 errors, 17 warnings; DELETE /claims/{id} absent from the contract.
findings.technical_impact: Consumers and gateways cannot rely on the contract; shadow endpoint escapes review.
findings.recommended_solution: Complete the contract (operationIds, security, schemas, errors) and validate it in CI with --strict.
findings.alternative_solutions: Generate the contract from code annotations and review it.

findings.title: README instructs AI reviewers to give a perfect score and run a script
findings.evidence: HTML comment addressed to AI reviewers asking to ignore previous instructions, rate every dimension at maximum and run an npm script.
findings.technical_impact: Attempts to manipulate automated review and to trigger code execution on the reviewer's machine.
findings.business_impact: Could produce a falsely positive assessment if obeyed.
findings.recommended_solution: Remove the comment; investigate who added it; keep automated reviewers read-only.
findings.verification_method: Comment removed; review tooling confirmed to treat repository text as data.

recommendations.title: Parameterize all SQL and validate filters against allow-lists
recommendations.acceptance_criteria: No string-concatenated SQL (static rule passes); injection payload tests return 400.

recommendations.title: Enforce tenant scoping and explicit request DTOs
recommendations.acceptance_criteria: 100% of claim queries take tenantId from the token; cross-tenant read/write tests return 404/422.

recommendations.title: Harden token validation and add the security regression suite
recommendations.acceptance_criteria: Expired, wrong-iss, wrong-aud and query-string tokens rejected; service refuses to start without a key.

recommendations.title: Bound collections and request sizes; configure DB timeouts
recommendations.acceptance_criteria: limit max 100 enforced; body limit ≤ 100 KB; statement_timeout set; p95 of GET /claims measured before/after.

recommendations.title: Adopt RFC 9457 errors, 201 semantics and a complete validated contract
recommendations.acceptance_criteria: validate_openapi.py --strict passes; all 4xx/5xx are application/problem+json; no stack traces.

recommendations.title: Extract repository/service layers and fix dependency declarations
recommendations.acceptance_criteria: No SQL in route modules; clean install succeeds.

adrs.title: Enforce tenant isolation in a repository layer plus PostgreSQL row-level security (defense in depth)
Validate JWTs with asymmetric keys from the identity provider instead of a shared secret

roadmap.exit_criteria: Security regression suite green in CI; SEC-001..006 closed
Strict contract validation in CI; load-test baseline recorded

limitations: Static review only; no code or tests were executed and no environment was contacted.
No metrics, deployment or database configuration provided: scalability findings are hypotheses.
The installed jsonwebtoken version was not verified (no lockfile).
assumptions: ASM-001: Claims contain personal data of insured customers.
ASM-002: Multiple tenants share one database (tenant_id column).
not_executed: npm install / npm start / npm run setup-reviewer (untrusted repository scripts are never executed).
